message.content:
Below are several ways you can pull out *detailed* information about a particular network interface (e.g., `eth0`, `enp2s0`, `wlan0`). Pick the method that best fits your environment (CLI vs. script) and let me know if you’d like a deeper dive into any of them. | Goal | Typical Command / Tool | What it shows | Notes | |------|------------------------|---------------|-------| | **Basic interface list & state** | `ip link show`
or `ifconfig -a` | Interface names, MAC address, MTU, link‑up/down status, driver name | `ip` is preferred on modern systems; `ifconfig` may not be installed by default. | | **IP addresses & routes** | `ip addr show eth0`
`ip route show dev eth0` | IPv4/IPv6 addresses, broadcast, scope, routing table entries for that iface | Use `ip -details addr show` for even more verbose output. | | **Hardware details** | `lshw -class network -short`
`sudo lshw -class network -numeric` | Driver, firmware version, bus info, physical location, capabilities | Requires root for full detail. | | **Driver & kernel module info** | `ethtool -i eth0`
`modinfo $(ethtool -i eth0 | grep driver | awk '{print $2}')` | Driver name, firmware version, module parameters | `ethtool` also reports supported speeds, duplex, autoneg settings. | | **Link statistics & errors** | `ethtool -S eth0`
`cat /sys/class/net/eth0/statistics/*` | RX/TX packet counts, error counters, collisions, dropped packets | Useful for troubleshooting performance issues. | | **Power management & wake‑on‑LAN** | `ethtool -a eth0`
`ethtool -P eth0` | Wake‑on‑LAN settings, MAC address persistence | | | **Network manager status** | `nmcli dev show eth0` | Connection profile, IP config, DNS, DHCP lease info | Works on systems using NetworkManager. | | **Python programmatic access** | ```python
import psutil
addrs = psutil.net_if_addrs()['eth0']
stats = psutil.net_if_stats()['eth0']
print(addrs)
print(stats)
``` | Programmatic retrieval of addresses, speed, MTU, flags | Good for scripts or dashboards. | --- ### Quick “one‑liner” cheat sheet ```bash # Show all interfaces + basic info ip link show # Show only one interface with all details ip -details addr show eth0 # Show driver & firmware ethtool -i eth0 # Show link stats ethtool -S eth0 # Show sysfs stats (alternative) cat /sys/class/net/eth0/statistics/rx_packets cat /sys/class/net/eth0/statistics/tx_errors # Show NetworkManager connection details nmcli dev show eth0 ``` --- #### Example output snippets 1. **`ip -details addr show eth0`** ``` 2: eth0: mtu 1500 qdisc pfifo_fast state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000 link/ether 00:1c:42:7b:8f:5e brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff inet 192.168.1.10/24 brd 192.168.1.255 scope global dynamic noprefixroute eth0 valid_lft 86399sec preferred_lft 86399sec inet6 fe80::21c:42ff:fe7b:8f5e/64 scope link valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever ``` 2. **`ethtool -i eth0`** ``` driver: e1000e version: 3.2.6-k firmware-version: 0.13-3 bus-info: 0000:02:00.0 supports-statistics: yes supports-test: yes supports-eeprom-access: yes supports-register-dump: yes supports-priv-flags: no ``` 3. **`ethtool -S eth0`** (partial) ``` rx_bytes: 123456789 tx_bytes: 987654321 rx_packets: 12345 tx_packets: 54321 rx_errors: 0 tx_errors: 0 ``` --- ### When to use each | Situation | Recommended tool | |-----------|------------------| | You just need to see whether the interface is up and its current IP(s). | `ip addr show eth0` | | You’re debugging connectivity problems (packet loss, errors). | `ethtool -S eth0` + `/sys/class/net/.../statistics` | | You need driver/module info (for updates or compatibility checks). | `ethtool -i eth0` | | You’re writing a monitoring script that needs to run on many hosts. | `psutil` in Python or `ip -json` for machine‑readable JSON | | You’re on a system managed by NetworkManager and want to see the active connection profile. | `nmcli dev show eth0` | Feel free to tell me which OS/distribution you’re on (Ubuntu, CentOS, Debian, RHEL, etc.) and I can tailor the exact commands or package names (e.g., installing `lshw`, `ethtool`, `net-tools`) for you.
